name: Question 7
problem: Consider the surface $z{x}^{3}=-1+x{y}^{2}.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(1,-2,3).$
worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}z{x}^{3} & =-1+x{y}^{2} \\ z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2}$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-1.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,-2,3):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =(3{x}^{2}z-{y}^{2})\text{ }i-2xy\text{ }j+{x}^{3}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(1,-2,3) & =(3(1)^{2}(3)-(-2)^{2})\text{ }i-2(1)(-2)\text{ }j+(1)^{3}\text{ }k \\  & =5\,i+4\,j+1\,k \\  & =⟨5,4,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,-2,3)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-(-2),\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨5,4,1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+2,\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ 5(x-1)+4(y+2)+(z-3) & =0 \\ 5x+4y+z & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Consider the surface zx3=−1+xy2. Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point (1,−2,3).

a
−x+y+z=0
b
5x+4y+z=0
c
3x+y+z=4
d
2x−4y+2z=16
e
x+2y+z=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we bring all variables to one side:

zx3=−1+xy2zx3−xy2=−1

If we set f(x,y,z)=zx3−xy2, our surface can be viewed as the level surface f(x,y,z)=−1.

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface f(x,y,z)=k at the point (x0,y0,z0) can be expressed as

∇f(x0,y0,z0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0.

Now, we find the gradient of f(x,y,z) and evaluate it at (1,−2,3):

∇f(x,y,z)=fx(x,y,z)i+fy(x,y,z)j+fz(x,y,z)k=∂∂x(zx3−xy2) i+∂∂y(zx3−xy2) j+∂∂z(zx3−xy2) k=(3x2z−y2) i−2xy j+x3 k∇f(1,−2,3)=(3(1)2(3)−(−2)2) i−2(1)(−2) j+(1)3 k=5i+4j+1k=⟨5,4,1⟩

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

∇f(x0,y0,z0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0∇f(1,−2,3)⋅⟨x−1,y−(−2),z−3⟩=0⟨5,4,1⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+2,z−3⟩=05(x−1)+4(y+2)+(z−3)=05x+4y+z=0
